title: Routing: integrate capacity signals (queue depth/scheduler lag) to drive admission control + priority under pressure
creator: Mina Haddad
body:
Context
We need routing to become “pressure-aware” so we can (a) preserve enterprise SLOs for protected routes during regional/fleet pressure and (b) throttle/shed best-effort traffic earlier and predictably. Gateway-tier rate limiting/quota (ENG-4922) reduces volume, but we still need a data-plane-aware gate that reacts to real capacity conditions (queue depth, scheduler lag, GPU saturation) and applies tier priorities consistently.

Scope
- Plumb capacity signals into routing service (per region, per pool/route-group).
- Use signals to enforce admission control for best-effort first, while preserving enterprise budgets.
- Provide deterministic, explainable decision logging and metric emission (low-cardinality).
- Feature-flagged, allowlist/region gated rollout with safe defaults + instant rollback.

Non-goals
- Scheduler fairness rewrite (we only consume exported signals).
- Billing or dynamic pricing changes.
- Per-tenant bespoke shaping beyond documented overrides (handled via policy engine + config).

Signal sources + contract
Primary signals (must be reliable, low latency, low cardinality):
1) runtime.queue_depth (by pool + route_group)
2) runtime.scheduler_lag_ms (by pool + route_group)
Secondary signal (use as corroboration only):
3) gpu.utilization_pct (by pool)

Implementation approach:
- Introduce CapacitySnapshot client in routing that fetches “capacity snapshots” from Fleet Signals / telemetry aggregation endpoint.
- Snapshot includes:
  - region
  - pool_id
  - route_group (e.g., chat, embeddings, rerank)
  - queue_depth_p95 / queue_depth_current
  - scheduler_lag_p95_ms / scheduler_lag_current_ms
  - generated_at + ttl_seconds
- Routing caches snapshot in-memory with TTL and falls back to “no admission control” when stale/unavailable (fail-open for enterprise; fail-soft for best-effort depending on pressure mode).

Admission control behavior
We gate at request admission (before selecting backend) using the following policy:
- Determine request class:
  - tier_class = enterprise | best_effort (from auth context + policy engine output)
  - route_group (from route mapping, not raw URL to avoid high cardinality)
  - pool candidate set (based on model + region)
- Determine pressure state per (region, pool_id, route_group):
  - NORMAL
  - PRESSURE
  - SEVERE
- Pressure evaluation uses hysteresis to avoid flapping:
  - Enter PRESSURE if (queue_depth_current >= QD_PRESSURE) OR (scheduler_lag_current_ms >= LAG_PRESSURE)
  - Enter SEVERE if (queue_depth_current >= QD_SEVERE) OR (scheduler_lag_current_ms >= LAG_SEVERE)
  - Exit only after sustained recovery window (RECOVERY_SECONDS) below lower thresholds
- Admission actions:
  - enterprise:
    - NORMAL/PRESSURE: admit
    - SEVERE: admit up to enterprise_budget (budgeted by policy engine route budgets); if budget exhausted, return 429 with reason=overload_enterprise_budget_exhausted
  - best_effort:
    - NORMAL: admit
    - PRESSURE: probabilistic shedding (configurable, default 10–30%) OR strict reject if shed_rate already high
    - SEVERE: reject early with 429 reason=overload_best_effort_shed

Notes:
- “enterprise_budget” is enforced via policy output (ENG-4923) and relies on consistent route_group mapping. This ticket is responsible for consuming the budget + capacity state in routing.
- We intentionally do NOT rely on raw GPU utilization as the primary trigger (too noisy / lags) per infra guidance; it’s only used to annotate pressure state and for debugging.

Determinism + auditability
- Decision logging (structured) emitted only on sampled basis to avoid overhead:
  - routing.admission_decision (sampled)
  - fields: region, route_group, tier_class, pressure_state, action(admit|reject|shed), reason_code, snapshot_age_ms
- Metric emission (low cardinality):
  - routing_admission_total{region, route_group, tier_class, decision, reason_code}
  - routing_capacity_snapshot_staleness_ms{region}
  - routing_pressure_state{region, route_group, pool_id, state}

Feature flags + rollout
- Flags:
  - hot_route_protection.routing_admission_control_enabled
  - hot_route_protection.routing_admission_control_allowlisted_accounts
  - hot_route_protection.routing_pressure_thresholds_overrides (region scoped)
- Rollout plan:
  1) Dark launch: fetch snapshot + compute pressure state, no gating; verify metrics.
  2) Canary: us-east, allowlisted enterprise accounts + limited best-effort shedding.
  3) Expand: additional regions after alert tuning and game day.
- Rollback: disable routing flag (immediate). If snapshot endpoint causes errors, routing client falls back to cached/stale data and stops enforcing severe actions for enterprise.

Acceptance criteria
- Under synthetic overload on chat route_group, routing sheds best-effort first while enterprise p95 latency remains within SLO target (validated during game day).
- No high-cardinality metric regressions (validated by telemetry review).
- Snapshot staleness alerts in place and exercised.
- Clear 429 reason codes propagated through gateway response schema (aligned with PR/Docs work).

Testing
- Unit tests: pressure state transitions (hysteresis), TTL cache behavior, allowlist logic.
- Integration tests: concurrent load with simulated snapshot updates; verify tier behavior.
- Load test: replay from traffic shape doc; verify shed rates & enterprise success rate.

Links / artifacts
- Confluence design: sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/hot-route-capacity-protection-technical-design.json
- Overload metrics standard: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/metrics-standard-overload-events-and-shed-reasons.json
- Runtime metrics ticket: ENG-4925
- Policy engine schema ticket: ENG-4923
- Feature flags: ENG-4928
- GitHub PR (routing): sources/github/redwood/pr-27427-routing-admission-control-using-capacity-signals.json

Owners / reviewers
- Eng owner: Elena Popov
- Routing TL: Mina Haddad
- Infra signal source: Vanessa Ortiz / Robert King
- SRE partner: Rafael Mendes / Peter Holtz

Open questions (resolved during implementation)
- Which signals are “authoritative” across regions? Resolved: queue depth + scheduler lag primary.
- Fail-open vs fail-closed when snapshots stale? Resolved: fail-open for enterprise, fail-soft (shed-only in SEVERE) for best-effort; no hard reject when snapshot unavailable.
- Threshold defaults: initial values set per region and tuned during us-east canary + game day; captured in config overrides.
comments: 2025-10-16 (Elena Popov): Kicked off with Infra + Runtime to align on signal availability and cardinality. Queue depth + scheduler lag are the only signals we trust for triggers; GPU util is too laggy/noisy for routing decisions. Action: define snapshot contract with Fleet Signals endpoint and ensure per route_group aggregation.

2025-10-22 (Vanessa Ortiz): We can provide aggregated metrics by (region, pool_id, route_group) at 10s cadence. Please avoid tagging by tenant/model_id on routing metrics; that will blow up. Suggest TTL >= 30s and a staleness metric so SRE can page if snapshot feed degrades.

2025-10-29 (Peter Holtz): Please add hysteresis + recovery window. Without it, routing will flap between admit/reject and cause retry storms. Also ensure best-effort shedding is reflected in a single counter with reason codes (quota vs overload) so on-call can quickly triage.

2025-11-05 (Elena Popov): Implemented CapacitySnapshotClient with in-memory cache + TTL and a dark-launch mode (compute pressure_state, no gating). Added routing_pressure_state gauge and snapshot staleness histogram. Preparing PR for review.

2025-11-08 (Mina Haddad): Review feedback: keep pool_id out of the admission_total metric (route_group + tier_class should be enough) and only emit pool_id for pressure_state. Also, make decision logs sampled and gated behind debug flag to avoid p99 overhead.

2025-11-14 (Rafael Mendes): SRE review: staleness behavior is good. For best-effort in PRESSURE, prefer probabilistic shedding rather than hard cutoff to reduce cliff effects. Make SEVERE a hard reject for best-effort. Enterprise should only reject when enterprise_budget exhausted (policy engine) to preserve contractual behavior.

2025-11-20 (Elena Popov): PR up for routing admission control: sources/github/redwood/pr-27427-routing-admission-control-using-capacity-signals.json. Includes hysteresis, TTL cache, allowlist, and reason codes wired through to gateway error schema. Needs final sign-off from Observability on metric names.

2025-11-26 (Logan Wright): Telemetry sign-off with minor rename to align with overload metrics standard. Confirmed labels are bounded: region, route_group, tier_class, decision, reason_code. No tenant/model tags.

2025-12-03 (Elena Popov): Merged PR-27427. Dark-launch enabled in us-east; no gating yet. Snapshot staleness is stable (<5s p95). No measurable routing latency overhead in canary (added ~0.15ms median).

2025-12-10 (Rafael Mendes): Enabled gating for allowlisted enterprise accounts + best-effort shedding in us-east during scheduled window. Observed best-effort 429 increase as expected; enterprise p95/p99 stable. One issue: SEVERE triggers too sensitive for embeddings route_group; tuning thresholds before expanding.

2025-12-13 (Elena Popov): Threshold tuning landed via config override (no code change). Embeddings SEVERE threshold moved up based on observed queue depth distributions. Added dashboard annotation for routing pressure transitions.

2026-01-08 (Mina Haddad): Marking Done. This is now the default routing behavior behind the project flag and is being rolled out region-by-region via ENG-4928. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-4931 for post-launch metrics review (watch for retry storms + unintended best-effort cliff behavior).
